motifs.name: Skeletal Gold
motifs.prose_description: A motif of gilded bone and ritual metalwork — gold filigree etchings over obsidian void surfaces, evoking gothic ceremonial objects. The filigree is never decorative filler; each line implies encoded data or structural constraint. Distinguished from Neural Neon by its warm temperature and architectural stillness rather than living luminescence.

motifs.name: Neural Neon
motifs.prose_description: Living networks of neon-lit synaptic connections rendered as node graphs, lattice topologies, and fractal tendrils. The dominant motif in the corpus — 789 of 1115 prompts. Distinguished by motion implied in static imagery: every image suggests flow, pulse, and directionality. Cyan and sync-blue are its primary channels.
avoid: static point lights with no directionality

motifs.name: Obsidian Membrane
motifs.prose_description: The negative-space foundation of the aesthetic: pure void-black surfaces with microscopic texture suggesting stretched obsidian or taut biological membrane. Not a background — an active skin. Light falls on it and is consumed. Distinguished from Skeletal Gold by the near-total absence of warm filigree; obsidian membrane is silent and absorptive.
avoid: high ambient illumination on void surfaces

motifs.name: Cyan Lattice
motifs.prose_description: Electric cyan grid-lines and luminous node halos floating in void space. The visual representation of data transfer and synchronization — every cyan line is a live signal. Distinguished from Neural Neon by its formal geometric register: while neural neon is organic, cyan lattice is crystalline and orthographic.
lean_into: zero-radius corners on cyan UI elements
avoid: warm color contamination of cyan channels

motifs.name: Magenta Bloom
motifs.prose_description: Saturated electric magenta erupts from void surfaces as reward blooms, multiplier orbs, and wild-state indicators. Always reads as exceptional — a state transition, not a base condition. Distinguished from Cyan Lattice by its emotional temperature: magenta is chaotic where cyan is structured.
avoid: using magenta as a background fill
magenta on any readable text surface

motifs.name: Cyber Terminal
motifs.prose_description: Hacker terminal aesthetics manifest as monospaced data streams, phosphor-green scan artifacts, and carved-stone interface panels that display real-time telemetry. The Gothic Hacker aesthetic's information-processing face: data as architecture. Distinguished from Neural Neon by its static, scanline-ridden character rather than fluid lattice flow.
avoid: overly animated or fluid motion in pure terminal contexts

motifs.name: Casino Glint
motifs.prose_description: The Vegas layer surfaces as oscilloscope volatility traces, neon casino typography, and specular gold glints on dark playing surfaces. This motif co-exists with Gothic structure: the game is a casino run by architects of the void. Distinguished from Skeletal Gold by its kinetic energy — Casino Glint is always in motion.
avoid: static gold surfaces without sparkle or motion

motifs.name: Bio Organic
motifs.prose_description: Bioluminescent veins pulse through biological-mechanical substrates — obsidian rock threaded with crimson vascular channels, icosahedron foliage balls glowing with internal light, bomb surfaces that breathe. The organic axis of the gothic-hacker axis ratio (0.32 organic from design_tokens.json). Distinguished from all other motifs by the presence of implied biology: these materials are alive.
lean_into: SSS (sub-surface scatter) on ice and organic tiles
avoid: cool blue temperature without organic warmth

creative_director_notes.topic: Canvas Configuration — Missing ACESFilmic and Shadows
creative_director_notes.prose: The current VoxelPileScene Canvas uses `flat` prop (disables tone mapping) and `antialias: false`. The `flat` flag overrides any tone mapping setting, so ACESFilmicToneMapping and SRGBColorSpace are not applied. The result is a scene where emissive materials look mathematically correct but aesthetically flat — bloom cannot build properly, HDR values in the wild-die and orb shaders do not tonemap to the target look. The immediate fix is to remove `flat`, add `gl={{ toneMapping: THREE.ACESFilmicToneMapping, toneMappingExposure: 1.1, outputColorSpace: THREE.SRGBColorSpace }}`, and add `shadows` prop. Ambient intensity should drop from 2.0 to 0.6 to restore depth under the new tonemap.

recommendations.label: implement_now
recommendations.text: Remove `flat` prop, add ACESFilmic tonemap, SRGBColorSpace, shadows, cap dpr at 2. Reduce ambient from 2.0 to 0.6. Add <Environment preset='city'> as baseline HDRI.

creative_director_notes.prose: No @react-three/postprocessing EffectComposer exists in the codebase. The wild-die shader emits HDR values (vec3(2.5,2.5,2.5)) explicitly to feed bloom — but without an EffectComposer Bloom effect, those values simply clamp to white with no glow. The multiplier orb emissiveIntensity=3.2 similarly has no bloom receiver. The minimum viable fix is Bloom + Vignette only (MC-2 Option A), which is mobile-safe and recovers the emissive budget already authored in the shaders.

recommendations.label: implement_now
recommendations.text: Install @react-three/postprocessing. Add EffectComposer with Bloom(luminanceThreshold=0.6, intensity=0.8) + Vignette(darkness=0.42). Mobile: same chain with reduced Bloom intensity=0.5.

creative_director_notes.prose: MultiplayerLobby.tsx uses '#0a1628', '#7ecfff', '#1a4060' — a completely different palette from the Gothic Hacker Neon system. This creates a jarring visual discontinuity when the player navigates to multiplayer. The palette needs to be unified to OV / GH tokens before the vertical slice ships. The cyan value '#7ecfff' is close to OV.cyan but at the wrong lightness, and '#0a1628' is a mid-blue rather than the correct '#050008' void.

recommendations.label: implement_now
recommendations.text: Retheme MultiplayerLobby.tsx to use GH palette (void, neural, bone, gold, cyan, acidLime) matching HomeScreen. Replace all hardcoded blues with OV token values.

creative_director_notes.topic: tokens.ts — Missing acidLime and syncBlue Keys
creative_director_notes.prose: The design_tokens.json requires acidLime (#c8d400) as the primary action color and syncBlue (#3388ff) as the network sync color. Both are present in local GH palette objects inside each component (HomeScreen, FarkleHUD, WinLoseScreen) but are absent from the canonical tokens.ts OV export. This means each component hardcodes the values independently, preventing the single-source-of-truth requirement. tokens.ts needs acidLime, syncBlue, and the full motion/typography token set from design_tokens.json.

recommendations.label: implement_now
recommendations.text: Add to tokens.ts: acidLime, syncBlue, full motion durations, easing curves, spacing scale, radius scale. Export CSS custom properties at :root from main.tsx.

creative_director_notes.prose: The current ChainLine renders as lineBasicMaterial color='#ffd700' — a flat gold line with no glow, no width, and no visual connection to the Phantasmagoric Chain vocabulary from the corpus (87 prompt references). This is the most visible placeholder in the game scene during active play. The chain is the primary interaction feedback element and must be upgraded to slice quality.

recommendations.label: implement_now
recommendations.text: Replace ChainLine with a tube-mesh or screen-space glow line using OV.cyan color, bloom-fed emissive value, and opacity pulse tied to chain length. Use useRef for positions to avoid React re-renders.

The 3.1% figure counts only the sample IDs explicitly listed in evidence blocks; the full motif support spans 284-854 samples each.
